Header:
Date: 2026-10-28
Start: 09:30 AM PT

Attendees: Ari Johnson (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (CTO, NexaHealth), Sofia Martinez (ML Engineer), Evan Cho (Security), Maya Patel (Infra)

Summary (auto): Weekly POC sync — onboarding progress, access setup, environment readiness, results review and tuning plan.
Topics: onboarding status; infra access (VPC, service accounts); tuning (batching, quantization, KV cache); bench next steps; security docs.

Transcript:
[00:00:05] Ari: okay hi everyone thanks for joining, um this is the weekly NexaHealth POC sync. quick roll call?
[00:00:12] Liam: hey, Liam here, CTO.
[00:00:14] Sofia: Sofia, ML eng.
[00:00:16] Evan: Evan, security.
[00:00:17] Maya: Maya, infra.
[00:00:20] Ari: and Ari from Redwood — and Priya's on for the SE deep dive.
[00:00:24] Priya: hi all, morning.
[00:00:28] Ari: alright first quick status — onboarding checklist, Maya, are we any closer on the VPC peering and service account?
[00:00:35] Maya: yes we created the peering request, uh there's a couple of firewall rules I need to confirm but I should be able to share the details by end of day Monday. i'm waiting on the network team to add the route for the 10.2.x range.
[00:00:47] Ari: great, that's in line with the timeline — we'll need the service account JSON and minimal IAM perms for the Redwood agent to run the bench. Sofia, any updates on the dataset and test harness?
[00:00:58] Sofia: yes I uploaded the sanitized test set to the S3 path we shared, it's about 8k prompts, mix of short clinical notes and long strings. i also pushed the testing harness repo link in the slack channel. one small thing — we saw tokenization differences between local run and Redwood's hosted run, some tokens are being split differently for clinical shorthand which slightly inflated token counts.
[00:01:20] Priya: yeah that's pretty common — tokenization differences, we can align on the tokenizer config; i'll pull a sample and show where the splits happen. tends to affect cost estimates more than latency.
[00:01:30] Liam: on cost, we still care a lot about unit cost — main KPI is sub-50ms p50 and cost below $0.0008 per inference for our 99th pct usage band — i know those are tight.
[00:01:42] Priya: understood. orthogonally we can trade batch size and quantization. for sub-50ms p50 it usually means smaller batches and potentially higher-spec instances; for cost we can try int8 quantization and larger batch windows but that'll add tail latency.
[00:01:57] Sofia: can you remind us what quantization profiles Redwood supports in the Dedicated/private runtime? we've been looking at 4-bit/8-bit options.
[00:02:06] Priya: sure — we support int8 and several 4-bit configs; the runtime has a quantization-friendly execution path but 4-bit can occasionally increase generation variance on longer contexts. we recommend int8 as first pass for production workloads; 4-bit is ok for internal evals if you accept some drop in quality.
[00:02:22] Evan: from security perspective, we need to make sure KMS integration is available before any private deployment. what is the flow for keys?
[00:02:30] Ari: Redwood Private integrates with customer KMS/HSM — we can either use our keywrap where customer provides key material in HSM or you can provision a key in your cloud KMS and we use a delegated service account. we'll share the SOC2 and keyflow diagram after the call.
[00:02:43] Evan: okay please share that. also for audit logs — how long do we keep the request/response logs by default?
[00:02:50] Priya: default retention on hosted is 30 days, but for Private you can configure retention; we also support forwarding logs to your S3 or SIEM for long-term retention.
[00:02:59] Maya: perfect, we plan to forward to our S3 with lifecycle rules.
[00:03:03] Ari: quick demo point — Priya, you had some recent bench results with kv-cache enabled vs disabled?
[00:03:09] Priya: yes i put snapshots in the bench spreadsheet; short summary — enabling prefix/KV cache reduced per-token compute by roughly 25% for our synthetic streaming workload and lowered p95 latency for repeated context calls, but warm cache is required. cold-starts still have same p95 baseline.
[00:03:26] Sofia: interesting — for our use case many prompts share patient context across calls, so prefix caching sounds promising. how does eviction work?
[00:03:34] Priya: we have an LRU policy and TTLs, and you can pin hot keys for critical workflows. memory footprint scales with cache size obviously; we'll recommend config based on your observed context reuse.
[00:03:44] Liam: ok next — infra readiness for the throughput run. Priya, what do you need us to open for the agents? ports, IPs?
[00:03:52] Priya: we need outbound connectivity from Redwood egress to your peered subnet, and inbound from our runner for the bench if you host the runner. service account with roles: compute.viewer and storage.objectViewer (min perms). also need a small firewall rule for the bench runner IPs, i'll list them in the support ticket.
[00:04:08] Maya: noted, we'll provision the role and update firewall after we get the exact IPs.
[00:04:12] Ari: timeline wise — if we get service account and peering by Nov 4 we can run a throughput test in the week of Nov 9. that run will mirror your production mix of 10k req/day and short/long prompt ratio.
[00:04:24] Liam: sounds good. any concerns about SLOs? we need a fallback path if Dedicated capacity can't hit the p95 targets.
[00:04:32] Priya: yes we discussed automatic fallback to hosted variants — Redwood routing can divert a percentage of traffic to a compatible hosted model automatically during peak or capacity events; that adds some latency but keeps availability. we can schedule a canary rollout test as part of the bench.
[00:04:46] Sofia: can we also test quantized model in the bench to compare quality deltas?
[00:04:50] Priya: absolutely, we'll include int8 and 4-bit runs and capture rouge/accuracy on your eval set.
[00:04:56] Evan: one clarification on data residency — some patient data falls under EU rules, is there a region pinning option for Redwood Private?
[00:05:02] Ari: yes, Private can be deployed in-region and you can pin routing by policy. for Hosted we also have regional endpoints but for strict residency Private is recommended.
[00:05:12] Liam: great. a couple of smaller items — we noticed tokenization mismatch earlier, can you put the tokenizer config in the repo so our preprocessing matches exactly?
[00:05:20] Priya: i'll add the tokenizer config and a small script to canonicalize your clinical shorthand.
[00:05:25] Sofia: thanks.
[00:05:27] Ari: ok let's walk through bench results briefly — Priya, can you summarize the numbers you posted?
[00:05:31] Priya: sure — baseline hosted run with no caching: p50 ~42ms, p95 ~180ms, cost roughly $0.0011 per inference on the sample. With Dedicated + int8 + KV-cache warm: p50 ~28ms, p95 ~120ms, cost ~ $0.0007. 4-bit reduced cost further but increased variance on long contexts (p95 climbed to ~220ms for some samples).
[00:05:55] Liam: ok so int8 on Dedicated hits our cost target, but p95 still above our desired. is that tunable?
[00:06:03] Priya: p95 is sensitive to sequence length and IO jitter; we can try smaller batch sizes for tail-critical endpoints, adjust autoscale config, and optimize kernel selection. also picking instances with higher memory per GPU can help reduce kv cache thrashing.
[00:06:17] Maya: are there recommended instance types for low p95?
[00:06:20] Priya: we typically recommend A100-class for low-latency p95; H100s do well at throughput. we'll include recommended SKU mappings in the bench sheet.
[00:06:30] Evan: about encryption in transit for peered traffic — are we using mutual TLS or VPC peering with subnet-level encryption?
[00:06:37] Ari: for Private deployments we support mTLS for control plane and dataplane can be put over private peering; additional IPSec layers can be added depending on the customer's requirements.
[00:06:46] Liam: ok good.
[00:06:48] Priya: i want to call out one gotcha — when you run the bench harness please set the same max_sequence_length as in production. if you use lower seq_len for bench we tend to under-estimate p95.
[00:06:58] Sofia: noted. we'll sync the configs.
[00:07:02] Ari: any blockers on permissions?
[00:07:04] Maya: only waiting on an IAM owner to approve the service account role, should be done by Monday.
[00:07:09] Ari: good. next — security review items? Evan?
[00:07:12] Evan: two items: need confirmation of RBAC for Redwood console access and proof of SOC2 Type II. also we need a network diagram showing data flows.
[00:07:22] Ari: i'll send the SOC2 snapshot and the network diagram. RBAC is configurable — we support SSO/SAML and granular project-level roles.
[00:07:30] Evan: do you have a default least-privilege role for engineers that only need observability?
[00:07:34] Priya: yes the "observer" role provides read-only dashboards and trace access without config or deployment permissions.
[00:07:41] Evan: good.
[00:07:44] Liam: let's make sure we have a final checklist — Ari can you recap?
[00:07:48] Ari: sure — 1) Ari to send updated bench spreadsheet + pricing + SOC2 and network diagram (due Nov 2). 2) Nexa (Maya) to share VPC peering, firewall rules, and service account (due Nov 4). 3) Priya to prepare test harness instructions & schedule bench (due Nov 6). 4) Run throughput bench week of Nov 9 and review results. 5) Priya + Sofia will run int8 vs 4-bit evals and capture quality metrics.
[00:08:18] Sofia: thanks, that works.
[00:08:21] Priya: one last technical clarification — if we run the bench against your dedicated cluster we may need a short maintenance window to prime caches; warm-up runs usually take 15-20 minutes.
[00:08:32] Liam: fine, we can allocate that.
[00:08:35] Ari: ok any other questions?
[00:08:38] Evan: just one on legal/procurement — we might need a short SOW for the dedicated trial, who do we engage?
[00:08:44] Ari: i'll loop in sales ops and legal after this call and share a draft SOW template.
[00:08:51] Liam: perfect.
[00:08:54] Priya: i'll also put the tokenizer script and bench config in the repo after the call.
[00:08:59] Ari: awesome, thanks everyone — we'll follow up in slack and email.
[00:09:05] Meeting ended.

Notes: transcript contains minor transcription errors typical of automated captions (names sometimes mis-attributed). Links referenced in call: bench spreadsheet (link posted in slack), tokenizer script (repo link), SOC2 snapshot (to be shared), network diagram (to be shared).
